title: From Weeping to Dancing
overview: A song of thanks from someone brought back from the edge of death, traditionally linked to the dedication of a house, though scholars are unsure which house or occasion is meant.

parts.label: Pulled back from death (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The depths, the grave and the pit are all pictures of death, so the singer is thanking God for healing when life seemed nearly over. Being spared also meant his enemies lost their chance to celebrate his downfall.

parts.label: Everyone join in (vv. 4-5)
parts.note: The singer calls God's faithful people to praise with him, because God's anger is brief while his kindness lasts a whole life. A night of tears giving way to morning joy is the psalm's picture of how short the hard times proved to be.

parts.label: Too sure of himself (vv. 6-7)
parts.note: When life was going well, he assumed nothing could ever shake him; the 'mountain' stands for his secure position, possibly his kingdom, which he admits was God's gift. When God hid his face, meaning God seemed absent, that confidence collapsed.

parts.label: Bargaining at the edge (vv. 8-10)
parts.note: He argues with God that a dead man is just dust and can no longer praise him or speak of his faithfulness. This reflects a common view in ancient Israel of the grave as a silent place where worship stops.

parts.label: Mourning turned to dancing (vv. 11-12)
parts.note: Sackcloth was rough cloth worn in grief, even by kings, so having it taken off and being dressed in gladness instead is a picture of sorrow replaced by joy. He says the point of being rescued is that his voice will keep praising and not fall silent.

think: When things have gone well for a long stretch, what happens to your sense of how secure you really are?
